quercus-alba.opening: A large, spreading tree whose seasonal story runs from spring flowers to autumn acorns.
quercus-alba.recognitionCue: Look for lobed leaves. A clear leaf photo is more useful for checking the match than a distant canopy.
quercus-alba.nextObservation: On an autumn visit, look for acorns and record what you actually see.

vaccinium-corymbosum.opening: Spring flowers, summer berries and changing autumn leaves give this shrub several moments to notice.
vaccinium-corymbosum.recognitionCue: Look for bell-shaped flowers and oval leaves, then compare the fruit when present.
vaccinium-corymbosum.nextObservation: Revisit the same shrub as flowers give way to fruit; note the plant’s stage rather than assuming a fixed date.

symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.opening: Summer-to-autumn flowers make this upright perennial worth revisiting as the season changes.
symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.recognitionCue: Look for purple or lavender flowers with yellow centres, rough leaves and upright clumps.
symphyotrichum-novae-angliae.nextObservation: Take a flower close-up and a leaf photo during bloom to help check the match.

berberis-thunbergii.opening: This dense, thorny shrub can carry red berries into winter—a useful feature to notice when checking its identity.
berberis-thunbergii.recognitionCue: Compare the small leaves and red fruit without handling the thorny stems.
berberis-thunbergii.nextObservation: Photograph leaves, stems and any fruit before deciding whether this is the invasive species.
